focus: memi-design mermaid-jam: parser diagnostics, ID normalization, revise pass
noveltyJustification: Nine findings are new and two corroborate earlier direction and skip-with-reason findings; (9 + 1) / 11 = 0.909.
keyQuestions: Which pre-write model check, rule set or validator does each corpus skill define before a FigJam write, and which of those rules are machine-enforced rather than advisory?

Which write route does each corpus skill use (hosted MCP `generate_diagram`, `use_figma` plugin API, console bridge, direct `fj`-style node script), and what read-back or verification follows the write?

Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?
answeredQuestions: Which pre-write model check, rule set or validator does each corpus skill define before a FigJam write, and which of those rules are machine-enforced rather than advisory?
How do the corpus skills handle Mermaid label and identifier hazards: emojis, reserved node IDs `end`/`subgraph`/`graph`, underscores in node IDs, and line breaks or markup?
ruledOut: Adopting Mermaid Jam's plugin as a Flow Mode route
Adopting ID rewriting into Flow Mode

label: Mermaid Jam is a local-only FigJam plugin that parses pasted Mermaid into native sections, cards and dynamic connectors, a sixth route and the only parser-first source.
Mermaid Jam's header diagnostic accepts TD, TB, BT, LR and RL, the strongest single counterevidence to Flow Mode's TD-only rule.
Mermaid Jam rejects styling constructs (classDef, class, style, linkStyle) with diagnostics, so Flow Mode's accent rule is only expressible on routes that support styling.
Mermaid Jam normalizes IDs to alphanumeric CamelCase and prefixes Step when needed, a third ID strategy alongside ompug's reserved-word suffix and Flow Mode's author discipline.
Mermaid Jam repairs labels by removing filler phrases and capping at 120 characters with a word-safe ellipsis, confirming long labels as a defect class even with no shared cap value.
The Revise pass normalizes arrows, adds a missing flowchart header, dedupes statements and quotes special characters, then re-parses before returning; Flow Mode has no repair pass.
The reviser refuses sources over 700 lines and tells the user to split them, a pre-work size gate Flow Mode lacks.
Generated output is always inside a FigJam section and manually moved node positions are preserved when IDs match, neither of which Flow Mode guarantees.
Diagnostics are line-numbered data returned before generation, and any error refuses generation, the third executable pre-write check in the corpus.
Unsupported Mermaid types return explicit diagnostics rather than bad output, corroborating skip-with-reason as a corpus norm.
Subgraphs are the corpus's unresolved construct: official supports two nesting levels, rocket-path recommends them, Mermaid Jam rejects them, and Flow Mode has no policy at all.

direction: Adopting Mermaid Jam's plugin as a Flow Mode route
reason: It is a consumer plugin with its own UI and no MCP surface Flow Mode could call.
